inputs.text: VEHICLE IDENTITY: ARES-01 is a large unmanned Mars science rover, not a car, truck, or SUV. It has exactly six identical airless metallic mesh wheels: three on the left side and three on the right, arranged as front, middle, and rear wheel stations. Each wheel has an open woven titanium-mesh structure, deep chevron tread bands, and a dark metallic hub. Low elongated rectangular chassis with angular white and light-gray protective panels. True six-wheel rocker-bogie suspension with clearly visible articulated linkages connecting all three wheel stations. Tall central camera mast with a rectangular stereo-camera head. One folded articulated robotic arm mounted on the front-right of the chassis. Compact high-gain antenna at the rear. Flat dark equipment deck covering the upper body. Subtle red ARES-01 mission markings. Functional aerospace engineering, scientifically plausible, realistic materials, no decorative fantasy or science-fiction technology. No pneumatic tires, no solid rubber automobile wheels, no hidden middle wheels, and never a four-wheel configuration. Preserve this exact design.

CAMERA VIEW: strict front-left three-quarter vehicle documentation view. The full rover is visible, camera approximately at rover height, rover large in frame. Precisely three same-sized, non-overlapping wheels are clearly visible along the near left flank: one at the front, one centered beneath the chassis, and one at the rear. At least two wheels from the far right flank are also visible in perspective. This is a NASA Mars-rover six-wheel layout, never a four-wheel terrestrial vehicle.

SETTING AND PHOTO STYLE: simple level Martian terrain, clear daylight, minimal atmospheric obstruction, no dramatic scene. This image defines vehicle identity; mechanical readability matters more than artistic composition. Photorealistic planetary expedition photography. Authentic NASA/JPL-style mission documentation with natural Martian illumination, physically plausible shadows, restrained colors, fine atmospheric dust, realistic optics and exposure, subtle sensor texture, and realistic Mars geology. No illustration, concept art, fantasy technology, or video-game-render appearance.
